prompt:
Now we are merging two PDDL domains into one domain. Please help judge whether two PDDL operators are equivalent.

domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action turn_left_on_meeting :parameters (?c ?other - entity) :precondition (and (traveling ?c) (traveling ?other) (left_turn_rule ?c) (near ?c ?other)) :effect (left_turn_rule ?c))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(left_turn_rule ?c - entity)': "entity ?c is in the state 'left turn rule'; used as effect of give_order, precondition of turn_left_on_meeting, effect of turn_left_on_meeting", '(near ?c - entity ?b - entity)': "relation 'near' holds; arguments: ?c is a entity, ?b is a entity; used as precondition of avoid_body, effect of avoid_body, precondition of turn_left_on_meeting, precondition of speak_to_meteor, effect of approach_sun, precondition of burn_up, precondition of arrest_meteor", '(traveling ?c - entity)': "entity ?c is in the state 'traveling'; used as effect of start_travel, precondition of avoid_body, precondition of turn_left_on_meeting, precondition of speak_to_meteor, precondition of approach_sun, effect of burn_up, precondition of arrest_meteor"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action wolf_promises_turnip_field :parameters (?p ?w - entity ?l - location) :precondition (and (alive ?w) (alive ?p)) :effect (plan ?p ?l))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(alive ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'alive'; used as precondition of send_sons_on_journey, precondition of ask_for_material, precondition of receive_material, precondition of build_house, precondition of wolf_knocks_and_requests_entry, precondition of pig_refuses_entry, precondition of wolf_huff_and_puff, precondition of wolf_blows_house_down", '(plan ?e - entity ?l - location)': "relation 'plan' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?l is a location; used as effect of send_sons_on_journey, effect of wolf_promises_turnip_field, precondition of pig_collects_turnips, effect of pig_collects_turnips, effect of wolf_promises_apple_orchard, precondition of pig_collects_apples_and_escapes, effect of pig_collects_apples_and_escapes, effect of wolf_promises_fair_trip"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".
